title: Woman
subtitle: Science has a gender. Food labels don't mention it.
description: Women's bodies respond differently to certain food ingredients. The evidence exists. It rarely makes it onto the label. BOTIA surfaces it.
why_body: For decades, nutritional and toxicological research focused on the general population — which in practice meant adult men. Women's specific biological vulnerabilities received less attention. BOTIA's Woman module is built on the evidence that does exist: peer-reviewed studies, EFSA opinions, WHO reports, and IARC classifications that document differential risk for women.
not_pregnancy_title: Woman is not a life stage
not_pregnancy_body: This module is not about pregnancy. It is not about motherhood. It is a scientific evidence layer that highlights documented risks relevant to women's biology — hormonal sensitivity, higher body fat percentage, endocrine vulnerability, and reproductive system exposure. It applies to all women, at any age.
two_types_body: BOTIA's Woman module works in two ways. When a specific ingredient with documented risk for women is detected on the label, BOTIA flags it directly. When no specific ingredient is found, BOTIA still surfaces contextual risk information — about packaging, about cumulative endocrine exposure, about fat-soluble compounds — because these risks exist regardless of what the label declares.
ingredients_body: These ingredients have documented evidence of differential risk for women's biology:
cards_body: These three signals appear regardless of the ingredient list — because the risks they describe are structural, not ingredient-specific:
card_endocrine_body: Cumulative exposure to substances that interfere with the hormonal system. Women are particularly vulnerable due to higher body fat percentage and hormonal complexity.
card_packaging_body: Chemical compounds that transfer from packaging into food — BPA, phthalates, PFAS. They do not appear on the ingredient list but enter the body through food.
card_fat_body: Lipophilic compounds accumulate in fatty tissue over years. They release during rapid fat loss, pregnancy, breastfeeding or menopause — in concentrated form.
can_1: Detect ingredients with documented differential risk for women.
can_2: Surface contextual risks that do not appear on the label.
can_3: Connect label ingredients to EFSA, WHO and IARC evidence specific to women.
cannot_1: Diagnose, assess personal risk, or replace medical advice.
cannot_2: Detect contaminants or packaging migrants not declared on the label.
cannot_3: Tell you what to eat or avoid — that decision is always yours.
closing: The science exists. BOTIA makes it visible.
source_note: WHO/UNEP State of the Science of Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals · EFSA BPA re-evaluation (2023) · IARC Group 1 classifications · EFSA phthalates risk assessment (2019)
